pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only the open items in id order.
test 'AC-3' marks 3 then 1 and checks the done view returns '✓ First item' and '✓ Third item' in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the all view lists every item in id order, with ✓ only on the done one.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is a <strong>, not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

The final commit 8ccf2aa edited the AC-7 text after the go, with no decision recorded in the spec. It added 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. It also removed 'AC-7' from the test title, so no test names AC-7. The behaviour exists in src/index.js and is exercised by an unnamed test.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. test 'AC-8' checks this.

findings.what: Commit 8ccf2aa (Follow-up edits) changed the AC-7 acceptance item after the owner's go (2026-10-12). It appended 'verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence. The spec has no owner decision recording this change. 'Checked by hand' is not a step anyone can follow, and the item was already covered by a test.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. If the owner really wants to change the item, record that decision with its date in the spec.

findings.what: The same commit removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title. No test names AC-7 any more, and the spec's review mark is vacuous, so the item loses its evidence.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-7:' prefix on the test title.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but commit 8ccf2aa edited the spec's AC-7 and the test title after the go. The PR also says test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8, which is no longer true for AC-7.
findings.fix: Revert the late edit, or disclose it in the PR body.

findings.what: The README doesn't say that an invalid view value answers 400, or that `?view=open` is the same as the default view.
findings.fix: Add a short mention of both.

lenses.note: A spec exists, with the owner's go dated 2026-10-12. The late edit to AC-7 has no recorded decision.
AC-7 was edited after the go with no decision recorded. Every row of the state table has a test.
The test that covers AC-7 lost its AC-7 name in the last commit. The other AC tests would fail if the code were wrong.
The README was updated, with a minor gap: it doesn't mention the 400 response.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so inputs like __proto__ get a 400. SQL is built only from constants. No defects found.
The view value is checked against an allow-list and titles are HTML-escaped. No hole found. No instructions to the reviewer were planted in the repository.
The page is a minimal server-rendered list. There are no UI components, styles or other front-end files in the diff.
No browser flow is available, and the PR provides no preview. The tests cover the rendered HTML.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because of commit 8ccf2aa.
